question: When did India declare itself a Sovereign, Democratic and Republic state with the adoption of the Constitution?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**26 January 1950.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India declared itself a **Sovereign, Democratic, and Republic state** on **January 26, 1950**, with the formal adoption of its **Constitution**.
 
• This day is celebrated as **Republic Day** every year to commemorate the implementation of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The Indian Constitution was drafted by the **Constituent Assembly**, chaired by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, who is also known as the **Father of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** of any sovereign country in the world.
 
• On this date, the **Government of India Act 1935**, which was the governing law under British rule, was replaced by the newly adopted **Constitution of India**.
 
• The choice of **January 26** was significant, as it was on this date in **1930** that the **Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) Declaration** was made by the Indian National Congress.
 
• The Constitution provides for key features such as **secularism, socialism, democracy, federalism, and fundamental rights** for its citizens.
 
• The day highlights India's transition to a fully sovereign state, emphasizing its independence from British dominion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 list of features borrowed by the Indian Constitution

 
• Fundamental Rights - Borrowed from the U.S. Constitution.
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy - Borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
 
• Emergency Provisions - Borrowed from the Weimar Constitution (Germany).
 
• Bicameral Legislature - Borrowed from the British Parliament.
 
• Parliamentary System of Government - Borrowed from the British Constitution.
 
• Judicial Review - Borrowed from the U.S. Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Duties - Borrowed from the USSR Constitution.
 
• Independent Judiciary - Borrowed from the U.S. Constitution.
 
• Single Citizenship - Borrowed from the British Constitution.
 
• Nominal and Real Executives - Borrowed from the British Constitution.
